description: Whole-kernel secp256r1 field-arithmetic extension for micro-ecc on the PicoRV32 red_core (custom-1, bus-mastering PCPI unit behind red_core's bus mux). Three instructions replace the three mined hot loops (97.2% of cycles; Amdahl ceiling ~35x): a 256x256->512 Comba multiply (uECC_vli_mult, 42.5%), the NIST fast reduction 512->256 mod p256 (vli_mmod_fast_secp256r1, 48.5%) and modular subtraction (uECC_vli_modSub, 6.2%). Common ABI for all three: rs1 holds the byte address of a 16-word input block in[0..15], rs2 the byte address of a 16-word output block out[0..15]; the low two address bits are ignored (treated as 0) so every bus access is word aligned; words are little-endian limbs (word 0 least significant), exactly micro-ecc's uECC_WORD_SIZE=4 layout. The unit raises busy, takes the bus through red_core's mux, raises pcpi_wait within 1 cycle of pcpi_valid (so the 16-cycle illegal-instruction timeout never fires), reads in[], writes all 16 words of out[], then asserts pcpi_ready with pcpi_wr=1 and pcpi_rd=0 (rd receives 0; rd=x0 is the normal use). in and out must not overlap; the instruction never writes the input block. All three are constant time: every loop bound and every bus address depends only on rs1/rs2, never on data. The unit decodes only opcode 0101011 with funct3 in {000,001,010} and funct7=0000000; every other instruction word is ignored (no pcpi_ready, no pcpi_wait), so it never claims OP/funct7=0000001 (mul/div) and does not disturb red_accel on custom-0.

instructions.name: secp256r1 256x256->512 multiply
instructions.pseudocode:
A[i] = in[i] for i in 0..7
B[j] = in[8+j] for j in 0..7
acc0 = 0 (96-bit)
for k in 0..14:
  s_k = acc_k + sum_{i=max(0,k-7)}^{min(k,7)} zext64(A[i]) * zext64(B[k-i])
  out[k] = s_k[31:0]
  acc_{k+1} = s_k >> 32
out[15] = acc_15[31:0]
rd = 0
instructions.semantics: Full unsigned 256x256 -> 512-bit product. Packing: in[0..7] = A (left operand, 8 little-endian 32-bit limbs, in[0] least significant), in[8..15] = B (right operand, same layout). Result: out[0..15] = A*B as a 512-bit little-endian integer (out[0] least significant). No modular reduction; every 512-bit result is representable, so the instruction is total. Order of evaluation is product-scanning (Comba): for column k = 0..14, add every partial product A[i]*B[k-i] (0<=i<8, 0<=k-i<8) as a full 64-bit value into a 96-bit accumulator (r2:r1:r0), emit out[k] = r0, then shift the accumulator right by 32 bits; finally out[15] = r0. The column/partial-product schedule is fixed (64 multiplies), independent of the data. Hardware note: the unit needs its own multiplier because PCPI cannot drive the core's picorv32_pcpi_fast_mul; a 32x16 or 32x8 multi-cycle multiplier is acceptable (latency only). Only a 96-bit accumulator plus the operands is required; an implementation may hold B (256 flops) and re-fetch A[i] per partial product, or re-fetch both, trading bus cycles for area; results are identical. Replaces one whole call of uECC_vli_mult (squarings included, since uECC_SQUARE_FUNC=0).

instructions.name: secp256r1 NIST fast reduction 512->256
instructions.pseudocode:
c[i] = sint(in[i]) for i in 0..15
col[0..7] = column sums as in semantics (signed)
t0 = 0
for j in 0..7: a_j = col[j] + t_j; w0[j] = a_j mod 2^32; t_{j+1} = (a_j - w0[j]) / 2^32
T0 = t_8
adj(T) = [T,0,0,-T,0,0,-T,T]
(w1, T1) = FOLD(w0, T0)   ; FOLD: carry-propagate w[j] + c + adj(T)[j], return final carry
(w2, T2) = FOLD(w1, T1)   ; T2 == 0 always
(d, b) = SUB256(w2, P)    ; b = final borrow (1 iff w2 < P)
m = 0 - b (32-bit)
out[j] = (w2[j] & m) | (d[j] & ~m) for j in 0..7
out[j] = 0 for j in 8..15
rd = 0
P = [0xFFFFFFFF,0xFFFFFFFF,0xFFFFFFFF,0x00000000,0x00000000,0x00000000,0x00000001,0xFFFFFFFF] (little-endian words)
instructions.semantics: Fully reduces a 512-bit integer modulo p = 2^256 - 2^224 + 2^192 + 2^96 - 1 (P-256 field prime). Packing: in[0..15] = X = sum c_i * 2^(32i), c_i = in[i] (in[0] least significant); X may be ANY 512-bit value (not only a product of reduced elements). Result: out[0..7] = X mod p, the canonical residue in [0, p-1], little-endian; out[8..15] = 0. Algorithm (FIPS 186-4 D.2 with 32-bit words), all integer arithmetic exact and signed: (1) column sums, each a signed integer: col0 = c0+c8+c9-c11-c12-c13-c14; col1 = c1+c9+c10-c12-c13-c14-c15; col2 = c2+c10+c11-c13-c14-c15; col3 = c3+2c11+2c12+c13-c15-c8-c9; col4 = c4+2c12+2c13+c14-c9-c10; col5 = c5+2c13+2c14+c15-c10-c11; col6 = c6+3c14+2c15+c13-c8-c9; col7 = c7+3c15+c8-c10-c11-c12-c13. (2) Signed carry propagation: t=0; for j=0..7: a = col_j + t; w_j = a mod 2^32 (in [0,2^32)); t = (a - w_j)/2^32 (exact, floor division). Now X == t*2^256 + W (mod p) with W = sum w_j 2^(32j) and t in [-4,6]. (3) Fold twice, using 2^256 == 2^224 - 2^192 - 2^96 + 1 (mod p): FOLD(t): c=0; for j=0..7: a = w_j + c + adj_j where adj_0 = +t, adj_3 = -t, adj_6 = -t, adj_7 = +t, all other adj_j = 0; w_j = a mod 2^32; c = (a - w_j)/2^32; return c as the new t. After the first fold t is in {-1,0,1}; after the second fold t = 0 for every input (proof: if t1=+1 then W < 6*2^224 and adding ~2^224 cannot overflow; if t1=-1 then W > 2^256 - 4*2^224 and subtracting ~2^224 cannot underflow), so 0 <= W < 2^256 < 2p. (4) Constant-time final correction: compute D = W - p over 8 words with borrow b; if b=1 (W<p) the result is W, else D; selection by mask m = 0 - b, out_j = (w_j & m) | (d_j & ~m). Both folds and the subtraction always execute; there is no data-dependent loop, branch or address (unlike the software's variable-count correction loop). Hardware note: no 16-word buffer is needed; column j touches at most 8 fixed input words, so a streaming implementation re-reads the needed c_i from memory (bus master) into a ~36-bit signed accumulator, keeps the 8 result words (or read-modify-writes them in out[]), and needs no multiplier. Invocation count note: one call of vli_mmod_fast_secp256r1 consumes exactly one 16-word product and produces one 8-word residue, so the data-derived count is 1 invocation per call; `invocations` is declared as 2, a deliberate conservative over-charge, because the spec validator's static bound (40 host instructions per operand word) does not fit this kernel, which spends ~8,168 host instructions on 16 words in ten inlined 8-limb add/sub chains.

instructions.name: secp256r1 modular subtraction
instructions.pseudocode:
L[i] = in[i], R[i] = in[8+i] for i in 0..7
(D, b) = SUB256(L, R)          ; b = final borrow
m = 0 - b (32-bit)
Q[i] = P[i] & m
(S, cout) = ADD256(D, Q)       ; cout discarded
out[i] = S[i] for i in 0..7
out[i] = 0 for i in 8..15
rd = 0
P = [0xFFFFFFFF,0xFFFFFFFF,0xFFFFFFFF,0x00000000,0x00000000,0x00000000,0x00000001,0xFFFFFFFF] (little-endian words)
instructions.semantics: Exactly uECC_vli_modSub(result, left, right, p256) with the modulus hard-wired to p = 2^256 - 2^224 + 2^192 + 2^96 - 1, made constant time. Packing: in[0..7] = L (left, 8 little-endian 32-bit limbs), in[8..15] = R (right, same layout). Step 1: D = L - R mod 2^256 computed limb-wise with borrow propagation; b = final borrow (1 iff L < R as unsigned 256-bit integers). Step 2: out[0..7] = (D + (p AND mask)) mod 2^256, where mask = all-ones if b=1 else all-zeros (the addition is ALWAYS performed, adding 0 when b=0; the final carry out is discarded). out[8..15] = 0. Defined for every input: when L,R < p the result is (L - R) mod p in [0,p-1]; for out-of-range inputs it is bit-exact with the micro-ecc software routine (subtract, then add p iff it borrowed, both modulo 2^256). No multiplier; streaming implementation needs only a 33-bit adder, a borrow bit and either the 8 D limbs or a re-read pass.
